thread:
alex: Quick proposal: I sketched a decision-tree for batcher topology + QoS handoff to unify admission paths across Hosted / Dedicated / Private. Sharing here for feedback. Diagram below.

priya: Nice — can you call out where KV-cache eviction signals live? That boundary's fuzzy in current flow.

alex: Good call. In the sketch eviction signals are emitted by the KV manager and consumed before admission. ASCII tree: 
```
incoming_request
├─ check: deadline_hint_ms <= 50 -> fastpath (no batching)
├─ else if streaming -> streaming-coalesce-lane (prefix-KV-check)
├─ else -> size/seq_len decision
│   ├─ small (tokens <= 64) -> microbatch-lane (tight-delay)
│   └─ large -> cohort-batcher (longer-delay)
```
Admission steps (topology):
  1) route-config eval (qos, fallback variant, max_batch_delay_ms)
  2) kv-cache probe -> if hit then short-circuit fast response
  3) admission policy (soft-reserve, tenant_quota check)
  4) enqueue to chosen lane/batcher
  5) preempt check & slot allocation -> execute

martin: Where does model-variant fallback fit? e.g. quantized fallback for cost SLOs.

alex: Route config should include explicit fallback fields. Example proto snippet: `qos.priority`, `fallback.model_variant`, `max_batch_delay_ms`, `deadline_hint_ms`. Decision tree uses `fallback` when admission denies full-capacity slot or when cost-policy triggers.

devon: Telemetry needs: per-route histograms for batch_size, wait_time, preemption_count, plus handshake events between admission stages. Suggest spans: `handshake.admission->batcher`, `handshake.batcher->executor`. Also emit `evict.signal.{tenant,reason}`.

samir: Two concerns: (1) per-tenant microlanes can cause head-of-line blocking; (2) elastic borrowing might starve small tenants when big tenant bursts. My suggestion: soft reservations + elastic borrowing capped by `borrow_limit_pct` and track `borrow_score` per tenant.

priya: +1. Also add canary rollout plan for topology changes: feature-flag behind 5% traffic, measure p50/p90/p99 latency and token-cost delta. Auto rollback if p99 latency regresses > 10% or error rate > 0.5%.

alex: Plan: I'll open an RFC follow-up with: decision-tree diagram, route-config proto, telemetry contract, canary plan, and an experiment checklist. Want volunteers to pair on prototype (measurement hooks + simplified admission). @devon @samir?

devon: :thumbsup: I can pair on the telemetry + experiment harness.

samir: I can take the admission policy prototype and borrowing algorithm.

alex: Great — I'll include a short integration test matrix in the RFC: eviction-signal ordering, fallback correctness, per-tenant fairness invariants, and canary rollback triggers.

devon: One more thing — scheduler-bot flagged a queue-depth spike on node-42 earlier that might be related to a stale admission rule. FWIW.
